pool.text: Explorers Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac and Alphonse de Tonty founded Fort Pontchartrain du Détroit.
Detroit began its civic history with its official incorporation and subsequent mayors.
The town of Detroit was first incorporated as a city before repeal.
The city held its first mayoral election featuring John R.
Detroit became the state's first capital following Michigan's admission to the Union.
Grand Circus Park was established as the city's first official municipal park.
The United Auto Workers labor union was founded in Detroit.
The Michigan Chronicle was established to serve as an African-American weekly publication.
The Huron–Clinton Metroparks system was established in the surrounding Metro Area.
The J. Westcott II vessel began its maritime operational service.
Louis Miriani began his tenure as the last Republican mayor of the city.
Motown was relocated to Los Angeles by Gordy to pursue film production.
Coleman Young was elected as the first Black mayor of the city.
The total number of homicides was officially documented.
The Metro Times weekly publication was founded to cover news and arts.
The elevated rail system known as the People Mover was completed for downtown service.
A movie was produced featuring the rock connections highlighted by the group Kiss.
Compuware completed its world headquarters in downtown.
Ernst & Young completed its office building at One Kennedy Square.
The renovated Lithuanian Hall reopened in the West Vernor area.
